research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (27 FR 727) prints Executive Order 10989 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1962-01-22; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Amendment of Executive Order No. 10168, of October 11, 1950, as amended, prescribing regulations relating to the right of enlisted members of the uniformed services to additional pay for sea and forei). I read the whole text and signature block. Inventory: the dossier's three clauses (the lead-in, the amendment adding clauses (5) and (6) to section 2(a), and the amendment of section 3 with the effective-date sentence) are contiguous and cover every operative sentence; I confirm the inventory as complete. The order further amends Executive Order No. 10168 of October 11, 1950, as amended (special pay for sea duty and duty at certain places for enlisted members): it adds two new clauses to section 2(a) treating duty on an artificial island such as a Texas Tower on the outer Continental Shelf as sea duty (clause 5 for assignment there, clause 6 for duty there while based ashore for eight consecutive days or more), amends section 3 to refer to clauses (3), (5) and (6), and states that the amendments are effective as of the first day of the first month after the month of issue, that is 1962-02-01. Ending: Executive Order 11157 of June 22, 1964 (29 FR 7973, Federal Register of June 24, 1964), section 502, states "The following Executive orders are revoked:" and its item (k) reads "(k) Executive Order No. 10989 of January 22,1962." Item (c) of the same section also revokes Executive Order No. 10168 itself. The held Federal Register text has no effective-date wording; the signature line's year is garbled in the OCR (it prints 1961 with a stray mark), but the same text prints "Filed, June 22,1964", the Federal Register issue is dated June 24, 1964, and the American Presidency Project record gives June 22, 1964, so I read the order as signed on 1964-06-22 and effective on signing. The alternative reading is the publication date, 1964-06-24. The cited source for the end is the complete held Federal Register text of EO 11157 (the dossier's located-provision records for this pair use a transcription mirror, which I did not rely on); section 502 is on its own lines in that text. Savings: EO 11157 restates the artificial-island clauses in its own section 202(a)(5) and (6) (it reads "While assigned to an artificial island (such as a Texas Tower)") and in section 203, and has no express savings clause (searched); pay accrued before the revocation is an accrued consequence. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit for this order), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).

savings.reason: The substance of the added artificial-island clauses was restated in sections 202(a)(5) and (6) and 203 of Executive Order 11157, which revoked this order; pay entitlements accrued under it before 1964-06-22 are accrued consequences. EO 11157 has no express savings clause in the held text, and no U.S. Code, eCFR or Federal Register catalog hit shows any other continuing effect of this order.
